sections.title: Canon precedence
sections.text:
1. Latest explicit user language and location corrections
2. Current AWS code, drafts, keyboard, and language rules
3. Current Drive source guidebooks and author approved atlases
4. Source-only revisions and older archived drafts used as reference evidence only

No older language counts are installed as active grammar.
No old TTRPG species or gameplay systems are installed into AWS.
No archived text overwrote saved book chapters, character records, dictionary or backend.
The Source Archive reader opens research data; it does not merge it into an editable manuscript automatically.
Duplicate Word and HTML guidebook exports are not multiplied into conflicting active pages.
Atlas records are structured but remain reference-only until approved.

sections.title: Protected Aza'raan canon
sections.text:
19 independent letters: ABDEGHIJKLMNOPRSTYZ
No independent U. Uh is in A family; old oo can use O-family accent.
Tzaphaer: taz-uh-fear
Belavados: bell-ah-vuh-doe-s
Arzuhan: are-zoo-hahn
Dakaroth: dack-uh-rawth
Belavados was destroyed by the Iron Dominion. The Aza'raan translation of Iron Dominion is not yet approved.

sections.title: Compatible historical notes
sections.text:
The original 52-glyph register is preserved as a historical source, not a 52-letter modern alphabet.

Historic source-only glyph simplifications were experiments, not approved replacements for the author's actual glyphs.

Contact references include Kaluseban, Azrahai, Gandirosha, Panolima, Gwynis, Geisamahi, Dril'thar, Tamhiogal, Jaspey, Aburata, Deorbasun and Volsarii. Source naming lists do not automatically change the approved roster.

Source documents describe a full eight-book saga and the 1351 BCE Cataclysm. Existing AWS manuscripts remain authoritative.

No invented Aza'raan translation for the Iron Dominion was introduced.

Tzaphaer is always pronounced taz-uh-fear, Belavados bell-ah-vuh-doe-s, Arzuhan are-zoo-hahn and Dakaroth dack-uh-rawth.
